item.question: Which CSS pseudo-class selects a parent element that contains a specific child?
item.reference_answer: The :has() pseudo-class. It matches an element if any of the relative selectors passed to it matches at least one element anchored at that element, so section:has(.featured) selects the sections that contain a .featured element.

item.question: How do I add state to a React component?
item.reference_answer: Call the useState Hook at the top level of the component, e.g. const [count, setCount] = useState(0). It returns the current state and a set function that updates it and triggers a re-render.

item.question: How do I declare a computed property with the Vue Composition API?
item.reference_answer: Import computed from vue and pass it a getter function, e.g. const message = computed(() => ...). It returns a computed ref (read with .value, auto-unwrapped in templates) that is cached and recomputed only when its reactive dependencies change.

item.question: How do I create a dynamic route segment in the Next.js App Router?
item.reference_answer: Wrap a folder name in square brackets, e.g. app/blog/[slug]/page.js, where [slug] is the dynamic segment; its value is passed to the page, layout or route handler in the params prop.

items.answer:
[1] Next.js Glossary – Next.js > Dynamic route segments

Route segments that are generated from data at request time. Created by wrapping a folder name in square brackets (e.g., `[slug]`), they allow you to create routes from dynamic data like blog posts or product pages. Learn more in Dynamic Route Segments.

[2] Dynamic Route Segments – Next.js

Use Dynamic Segments to read URL path params and generate routes from dynamic data.

A URL path is a sequence of path segments. In the App Router, a segment may be **static** (a literal value matched exactly) or **dynamic** (a placeholder that captures a value from the URL). When you don't know a segment's value ahead of time, define a Dynamic Segment to create routes from dynamic data. Next.js passes the captured values to your page via the path `params` prop, either filled in at request time or prerendered at build time.

> **Good to know**: Dynamic Segments are often referred to as path params, route params, or URL params.

[3] Dynamic Route Segments – Next.js > Convention

Dynamic Segments are passed as the `params` prop to `layout`, `page`, `route`, and `generateMetadata` functions.

| Route                     | Example URL | `params`        |
| ------------------------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `/blog/a`   | `{ slug: 'a' }` |
| `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `/blog/b`   | `{ slug: 'b' }` |
| `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `/blog/c`   | `{ slug: 'c' }` |

Dynamic segments that appear before the root layout are **root parameters**, which can additionally be read from any Server Component with `next/root-params`.

item.question: What does the useState composable do in Nuxt?
item.reference_answer: It creates a reactive, SSR-friendly shared state identified by a unique key, e.g. useState('counter', () => 0). The value is shared between components and kept from server rendering to hydration; because it is serialized to JSON, it must not contain classes, functions or symbols.

items.answer: [1] useState – Nuxt The useState composable creates a reactive and SSR-friendly shared state. [2] State Management – Nuxt Nuxt provides powerful state management libraries and the useState composable to create a reactive and SSR-friendly shared state. Nuxt provides the `useState` composable to create a reactive and SSR-friendly shared state across components. `useState` is an SSR-friendly `ref` replacement. Its value will be preserved after server-side rendering (during client-side hydration) and shared across all components using a unique key. **Important:** Because the data inside `useState` will be serialized to JSON, it is important that it does not contain anything that cannot be serialized, such as classes, functions or symbols. Read more about `useState` composable. [3] State Management – Nuxt > Shared State By using auto-imported composables we can define global type-safe states and import them across the app. ```ts twoslash [composables/states.ts] export const useColor = () => useState('color', () => 'pink') ``` ```vue [app/app.vue] ```

item.question: What is a union type in TypeScript?
item.reference_answer: A type formed from two or more other types, written with |, such as number | string; a value may be any one of the member types. Only operations valid for every member are allowed until the value is narrowed.

item.question: Hogyan kérek le adatot szerveroldalon Next.js App Routerben?
item.reference_answer: Server Componentben: a komponenst async függvénnyé kell alakítani, és abban await-tel meghívni a fetch API-t (vagy egy ORM-et, adatbázist), pl. export default async function Page() { const data = await fetch(...) }.

item.question: Mire való a React useEffect hookja?
item.reference_answer: A useEffect egy React Hook, amellyel a komponenst egy külső rendszerrel szinkronizáljuk (pl. hálózat, böngésző API, harmadik féltől származó widget): a setup függvény a renderelés után fut, a cleanup függvény pedig a függőségek változásakor és a komponens eltávolításakor.

item.question: How do I fetch data on the server in Next.js and in Nuxt, and what is the difference?
item.reference_answer: Next.js App Router: make a Server Component async and await fetch (or an ORM or database) in it. Nuxt: use the useFetch or useAsyncData composables (built on $fetch), which run on the server and forward the data to the client, so it is not fetched twice during hydration. The difference: Next.js fetches in async Server Components, Nuxt through composables in universal rendering.

item.question: Mi a különbség a React useState és a Nuxt useState között?
item.reference_answer: A React useState egy Hook, amely egy komponens saját állapotváltozóját adja vissza egy setter függvénnyel együtt ([state, setState]). A Nuxt useState egy kulccsal azonosított, SSR-barát, komponensek között megosztott reaktív állapot (ref), amely a szerveroldali renderelés után a kliensre is átkerül, ezért JSON-ba szerializálhatónak kell lennie.

items.answer:
[1] State Management – Nuxt

Nuxt provides powerful state management libraries and the useState composable to create a reactive and SSR-friendly shared state.

Nuxt provides the `useState` composable to create a reactive and SSR-friendly shared state across components.

`useState` is an SSR-friendly `ref` replacement. Its value will be preserved after server-side rendering (during client-side hydration) and shared across all components using a unique key.

**Important:**
Because the data inside `useState` will be serialized to JSON, it is important that it does not contain anything that cannot be serialized, such as classes, functions or symbols.

Read more about `useState` composable.

[2] useState – Nuxt > Type

```ts [Signature]
export function useState<T> (init?: () => T | Ref<T>): Ref<T>
export function useState<T> (key: string, init?: () => T | Ref<T>): Ref<T>
```

- `key`: A unique key ensuring that data fetching is properly de-duplicated across requests. If you do not provide a key, then a key that is unique to the file and line number of the instance of `useState` will be generated for you.
- `init`: A function that provides initial value for the state when not initiated. This function can also return a `Ref`.
- `T`: (typescript only) Specify the type of state

[3] useState – Nuxt

The useState composable creates a reactive and SSR-friendly shared state.

item.question: Is #777777 text on a white background readable enough for WCAG AA?
item.reference_answer: The contrast ratio is 4.47:1. It fails WCAG AA for normal text (at least 4.5:1) and passes only for large text (at least 3:1); it also fails AAA.

items.answer:
[1] Color contrast – MDN > Related WCAG success criteria

- 1.4.3 Minimum contrast (AA)
    The color contrast between background and foreground content should be at a minimum level to ensure legibility:
    - Text and its background should have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
    - Heading (or just larger) text should have a ratio of at least 3:1. Larger text is defined as at least 18pt, or 14pt bold.

- 1.4.6 Enhanced contrast (AAA)
    This follows, and builds on, criterion 1.4.3.
    - Text and its background should have a contrast ratio of at least 7:1.
    - Heading (or just larger) text should have a ratio of at least 4.5:1.

- 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast (AA)
    There should be a minimum color contrast ratio of 3 to 1 for user interface components and graphical objects.

[2] Color contrast – MDN

When designing readable interfaces for different vision capabilities, the WCAG guidelines recommend the following contrast ratios:

| Type of content                                                                 | Minimum ratio (AA rating) | Enhanced ratio (AAA rating) |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Body text                                                                       | 4.5 : 1                   | 7 : 1                       |
| Large-scale text (120-150% larger than body text)                               | 3 : 1                     | 4.5 : 1                     |
| Active user interface components and graphical objects such as icons and graphs | 3 : 1                     | Not defined                 |

item.question: Which selector has the higher specificity: `#nav a` or `.menu li a`?
item.reference_answer: #nav a has specificity (1, 0, 1) and .menu li a has (0, 1, 2), so #nav a is more specific: one ID outweighs any number of classes and type selectors.

item.question: Is the :has() pseudo-class supported in Safari 15?
item.reference_answer: No. Safari supports :has() from version 15.4, so Safari 15.0 does not support it.

item.question: Működik a `:has()` szelektor a Firefox 115-ben?
item.reference_answer: Nem. A Firefox a 121-es verziótól támogatja a :has() pszeudo-osztályt, így a 115-ös verzióban nem működik.

item.question: Melyik a nagyobb kontrasztú: fekete szöveg #f5f5f5 háttéren, vagy #595959 szöveg fehér háttéren? Megfelelnek a WCAG AA-nak?
item.reference_answer: Fekete szöveg #f5f5f5 háttéren 19,26:1, #595959 szöveg fehér háttéren 7,0:1, tehát a fekete szöveg kontrasztja nagyobb. Mindkettő megfelel a WCAG AA-nak normál szövegnél is (legalább 4,5:1), sőt az AAA-nak (legalább 7:1) is.
item.notes: Two contrast checks in one question: the planner should run the tool twice.
